sources.title: LAY'S Heartwork Microinfluencer Report - Heartwork Packs - 18.09.2020
sources.content:
LAY’S #HEARTWORK PACKS TO MICRO INFLUENCERS
1st July – 14th September 2020

THE BRIEF
Building on the connect formed with close to 1500 micro-influencers from the Smile campaign, LAY’S continued the trend by introducing LAY’S #Heartwork special packs to the extended LAY’S family securing reach, awareness, engagement and brand love.

Furthermore, the idea was to ensure every corner of India learnt of the LAY’S #Heartwork campaign through multiple social media posts that showered gratitude and drove donations for the unsung heroes of the country – farmers, truck drivers, retailers and many more.

OUR APPROACH
3 box & cotton pack types
Designing + printing
Buying lays packs
INR 20 pack
Special note as per pack type
Designing + printing
Corrugated box
To protect the box
Courier
All India Under Covid19 lockdown
Coordinating with the influencers
Calling to ensure messaging comes across

On connecting with the overall database of influencers we saw immense interest to participate in the campaign.
We connected with each of them individually and briefed them on the LAY’S #Heartwork Campaign and urged them to spread the word on their social media pages.

Alongside the outreach, we worked on preparing over 1000 LAY’S Heartwork boxes with customized letters and LAY’S Heartwork packs for each influencer, which was then shipped to their personal address amid a partial lockdown.
After the deliveries were made, we individually connected with each of them for feedback.

PHASE 1
1st July – 20th August
Total Packs Sent: 900
Promised Engagement: 700
Total Influencers engaged: 737
Posts Done: 587
Stories Done: 506

PHASE 2
20th August – 14th September
Total Packs Sent: 500
Promised Engagement: N/A
Total Influencers engaged: 321
Posts Done: 266
Stories Done: 379

TOTAL
Total Packs Sent: 1400
Total Influencers engaged: 1058
Posts Done: 853
Stories Done: 885

RESULTS
Tracked as per listening tool (excludes stories without hashtag/brand handle).
Reached out to 1400 influencers for the activity.
75% of the influencers organically posted on Instagram – 1058 influencers.
On an average each Influencer did 1 Instagram post & 3-4 Instagram stories.

CAMPAIGN PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
ENGAGEMENT: 3.81 M
REACH: 4.76 M
MICRO INFLUENCERS: 1058 activated
POSTS/VIDEOS: 1738 (posts + stories)
Total Activity Duration: 1st July – 14th September 2020
Tracked as per listening tool (excludes stories without hashtag/brand handle).

CAMPAIGN PERCEIVED VALUE & COST SAVING
Perceived total amount: INR 1,58,72,000.
By doing Barter campaigns brand spent INR 14 Lakhs all inclusive.
Compared with the perceived value of INR 158 Lakhs.
Saving done by the brand: INR 1.44 Crore.

KEY LEARNINGS AND TAKEAWAYS
What Worked:
All influencers loved the campaign thought and appreciated how LAY’S urged other brands to thank the unsung heroes.
Influencers were elated to receive a repost from the brand handle.
Corrugated boxes helped provide extra protection during mass delivery.
Everyone followed the brief & tagged & thanked people personally as well.
Lot of fan engagement came and phase 2 was done out of sheer demand.

What Didn’t Work:
Influencers were slightly unclear about the cotton packs. Would recommend printing - DO NOT OPEN at the back of the pack.
Couriers were delayed under lockdown in certain areas.
Under COVID19 social distancing packaging teams had to work overtime.
Influencers who didn’t post wanted more than 1 pack of chips in the barter or wanted a payment for their post.
sources.notes: First-party report. Metric scope and later/earlier report conflicts must be resolved by the evidence pipeline.

sources.title: Lay’s Heartwork x Reels Brief 22 July 2020
sources.content:
Lay’s Heartwork x Reels Brief | 22 July 2020

Idea
We launched our #Heartwork campaign to thank our unsung heroes such as farmers, factory workers, delivery people, shopkeepers and more who work tirelessly to bring us joy. We also thanked the Heartworkers of other brands on Twitter and Instagram, who are doing #Heartwork to make moments of joy possible.

Through Reels, we want people to express their gratitude towards the Heartworkers of their choice through our #Heartwork anthem. We’ll upload original music clips of our Heartwork anthem and #Heartwork stickers which will be used to create interesting content thanking the Heartworkers.

Mandates
Use campaign hashtags including #LaysIndia and #Heartwork and tag @lays_india.
Record performance in apparel matching the brand colour yellow.
Do not use hate symbols or political or religious references.
No competitor brand should be visible in frame.
Do not trivialize the contribution of those doing #Heartwork.
Choose one or more professions and thank their workers through the performance.

Creative Directions
The Heartwork Dance: enact actions of the Heartworker being thanked and include the heart symbol made with hands.
Lip Sync: expressive performance; additional actors may be used.
Acting It Out: a simple set thanking Heartworkers can be explored.
Creators were free to develop concepts as long as they followed the mandates.

reconciliationAuditResult.summary: The ledger is publication-safe overall, but reconciliation was overly conservative in two areas: it treated several mutually compatible activity metrics as one unresolved conflict, and it failed to use the explicitly supported total activity duration to corroborate the years of the two phase date ranges.

findings.message: The content-average-counts group incorrectly treats all included metrics as mutually inconsistent. Claims 018 and 026 report compatible versions of the same 1,058-influencer result, while claims 019 and 020 sum exactly to claim 027's 1,738 combined items. Claim 027 also expressly identifies a listening-tool tracking boundary. The clear numerical tension arises principally from claim 023's per-influencer averages; claim 022's generic statement that influencers 'posted on Instagram' does not necessarily mean each produced a feed post. Grouping and withholding every metric obscures these compatibility and scope distinctions.

The withholding rationale for the phase date claims considers only their isolated excerpts and overlooks claim 028, which explicitly establishes the overall activity period as 1 July to 14 September 2020. The Phase 1 and Phase 2 ranges fall exactly within and partition that supported 2020 activity duration, providing strong global corroboration for the year that reconciliation did not address.

architecture.narrativeThesis: LAY’S #Heartwork can be presented as a high-touch influencer activation that drew on an existing micro-influencer network to spread gratitude for India’s unsung heroes. Its strongest evidence-backed story combines individualized creator outreach, structured creative guidance, lockdown-era fulfilment and carefully scoped performance and value reporting.
architecture.storyStrategy: Build the story around the activation system rather than forcing a generic challenge-to-solution arc. Begin with the campaign’s gratitude purpose, establish the inherited creator relationship, and then separate the documented micro-influencer outreach from the planned Reels creative framework. Follow with the operational realities of delivering at scale during partial lockdown, the feedback and adaptation loop, and finally the listening-tool results and report-defined economics. Distinguish outreach, packs sent and tracked performance rather than implying they share a one-to-one denominator.

chapters.purpose: Detail the one-to-one briefing and follow-up model, then quantify outreach and distribution as separate activity measures.

chapters.purpose: Explain the planned participation mechanic: creators could choose professions and concepts while working within the anthem, sticker, tagging, hashtag and brand-colour mandates. Keep this framed as the documented Reels plan rather than claiming unsupported execution results.

chapters.purpose: Show what physical activation required during partial lockdown: customized letters and packs, protective corrugated packaging, shipment to personal addresses, packaging-team overtime and courier delays.

chapters.purpose: Present the report’s positive reactions alongside the demand attributed to fan engagement, the cotton-pack clarification recommendation and the stated reasons some influencers did not post. This creates a balanced learning chapter rather than an unqualified success claim.

architecture.designRationale: A flexible editorial treatment is stronger than a standard linear template because the evidence supports several distinct dimensions: campaign purpose, an inherited creator relationship, a documented outreach operation, a planned Reels mechanic, lockdown logistics, qualitative feedback, scoped performance and report-defined economics. The structure keeps those evidence types separate and prevents planned creative guidance from being presented as executed output. It also avoids the low-confidence creator and content totals, preserves the listening-tool limitations, and treats the economic figures as report language rather than audited ROI. This produces a more credible case study than forcing every detail into a simplified challenge-insight-idea-outcome sequence.

sections.heading: A nationwide invitation to thank the people who kept everyday life moving
sections.body: LAY’S #Heartwork invited social participation around gratitude for unsung heroes—including farmers, factory workers, delivery people and shopkeepers—with the stated aim of spreading awareness across India and encouraging donations. The campaign also thanked the Heartworkers of other brands on Twitter and Instagram.

sections.heading: An existing micro-influencer connection became the starting point
sections.body: The activity drew on a connection formed with close to 1,500 micro-influencers during the earlier Smile campaign.

That documented relationship provided the foundation for the #Heartwork micro-influencer activity. It established a known creator network without assuming any broader continuity between the two campaigns.

sections.heading: Individual outreach was the operational core
sections.body: From 1 July to 14 September 2020, the team connected with influencers individually, briefed them on #Heartwork and encouraged them to spread the campaign through their social pages.

The one-to-one model continued after delivery, when the team contacted influencers individually for feedback. Outreach and physical distribution were documented as separate activity measures and should not be treated as sharing a one-to-one denominator.

sections.heading: Two distinct measures of activity scale

items.label: Influencers reached out to
items.note: Direct outreach total; not automatically equivalent to packs sent, creators activated or tracked posters.

items.label: Packs sent across the activity
items.note: Physical distribution total; no one-pack-per-influencer relationship is inferred.

sections.heading: Structured freedom for creator-led gratitude
sections.body: The documented Reels plan asked people to express gratitude to Heartworkers of their choice through the #Heartwork anthem, while giving creators room to develop their own concepts within defined campaign mandates.

Creators could choose one or more professions to thank and work from three proposed directions: Heartwork Dance, Lip Sync or Acting It Out. The plan called for original anthem clips and #Heartwork stickers, along with required use of #LaysIndia and #Heartwork, a tag for @lays_india and apparel matching the brand colour yellow. These elements describe the planned brief rather than verified execution results.

sections.heading: Physical activation required hands-on fulfilment under constraint
sections.body: Amid a partial lockdown, the team prepared more than 1,000 Heartwork boxes with customized letters and packs, then shipped them to influencers’ personal addresses.

Corrugated boxes provided extra protection during mass delivery. Behind the packs, packaging teams worked overtime under COVID-19 social-distancing conditions, while couriers faced delays in certain lockdown-affected areas.

sections.heading: Creator response offered encouragement—and operational feedback
sections.body: The report says influencers appreciated the campaign thought and LAY’S encouraging other brands to thank unsung heroes. It also says creators were elated when the brand handle reposted their content.

The report attributes Phase 2 to demand following fan engagement. It also records uncertainty about the cotton packs, leading to a recommendation that a warning be printed on the back. For influencers who did not post, the report cites requests for more than one pack of chips in the barter or payment for a post.

sections.heading: Reach and engagement, within a defined listening boundary
sections.body: Listening-tool reporting captured campaign reach and engagement but excluded stories that did not contain a hashtag or brand handle.

semanticCritic.summary: The finished case study is semantically sound and draft-ready. It follows the approved activation-system architecture, clearly separates outreach from pack distribution, distinguishes the planned Reels framework from verified execution, preserves listening-tool limitations, and attributes the economic figures to the source without recasting them as audited ROI. No material evidence, scope, continuity, metric, narrative, or omission issues were identified.
